title: kv-cache: adaptive memory rebalancer and spillover paging improvements
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: production KV cache has continued to suffer from cross-shard fragmentation and high-frequency full-eviction events under mixed chat workloads which hurt throughput and increased cold token latency. This PR implements an adaptive memory rebalancer plus safer spillover/paging semantics to reduce fragmentation and make spillover to host memory less disruptive to latency-sensitive requests. Motivation: reduce the frequency and cost of aggressive evictions, improve long-running chat session hit rates, and enable long tail stability during load spikes. Design summary: 1) Adaptive memory rebalancer: background rebalancer thread per-GPU that monitors per-shard fragmentation_ratio, live KV occupancy, and recent eviction counts and runs low-priority compaction passes when fragmentation exceeds thresholds. Rebalancer uses a cost model that weights contiguous-run reclamation higher to produce kernel-friendly allocations and reduce future allocation work. 2) Spillover paging path: when memory is exhausted we now perform paged spillover to host RAM with async prefetch and prioritized eviction lanes. Hot items are promoted to a fast lane; cold items spill to a compressed page store. The paging implementation is cooperative with the serving scheduler: spill/readback IOs are scheduled with budgeted tokens to avoid blocking critical inference batches. 3) Eviction policy changes: switch from purely global LRU to an eviction priority that factors in recent access recency, token-length heuristics, and shard-criticality. This reduces noisy-neighbor evictions. 4) Online defragmentation and compaction: lightweight in-place compaction that preserves KV IDs and uses copy-on-write when necessary to avoid corruption. 5) Observability and feature gating: new metrics and feature flags so we can roll out progressively and measure regressions. Tests and rollout: unit tests for allocator invariants and paging paths were added, integration canary in perf lab with 3-stage rollout behind a feature flag, and rollback plan included. Performance: on staging with a mixed-length chat workload (70% short, 30% long contexts) we observed a 6-12% increase in sustained throughput on single-GPU nodes and a 28-35% reduction in full-eviction events that previously triggered expensive reloads. 99th-percentile token latency is unchanged within measurement noise (+0.5ms). Safety: rebalancer runs with low CPU/GPU priority and has a jittered backoff to avoid synchronization with autoscaler events. Related: builds on prior spillover work (see PRs 216789, 220345, 224568) and addresses ENG-4123. This description includes implementation details, testing notes, and rollout guidance so reviewers can validate safety and performance. The description is intentionally single-line to match PR export conventions.
commits: 7 commits: initial rebalancer prototype; allocator refactor; paging path and async IO; eviction priority adjustments; metrics and flags; unit tests; benchmark harness updates.
review_comments: Markus Li: Please add explicit invariants for allocator during compaction and a stress test for concurrent access. Response: added allocator invariants and a stress test (test_rebalance.py) that runs in CI canary.

perf_summary: Staging perf lab (p3-standard equivalent), mixed chat workload: sustained throughput +6-12% depending on shard mix, full-eviction events decreased 28-35%, memory fragmentation_ratio reduced from median 0.42 to 0.18, spillover IO increased but p99 IO latency kept below 8ms with async prefetch. Tail token latency unchanged within 0.5ms.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory rebalancer to reduce fragmentation and reduce full-eviction frequency
Introduced paged spillover path with async prefetch and IO budgeting to reduce latency impact of spillover
Rollout behind feature flag; safe gradual enablement recommended for Dedicated clusters
